Marvin Wilson Tabor Associate Professor of Environmental Health 11/24/44

Emory & Henry College, Emory, VA	B.S.	1966	Chemistry
Marshall University, Huntington, W.VA	M.S.	1968	Phys. Org. Chem.
University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, OH	Ph.D.	1974	Biol.Chem./Microbiol.
Veterans Administration Medical Center	Postdoc	1976	Analyt.Chem./Microbiol.

Experience:

1976-78: Supervisor of Lab. Services, Maternal and Infant Care, and Research Assoc., Dept. Ob/Gyn, University of Cincinnati College of Medicine

1978-79: Research Assoc., Dept. Environ. Hlth., Univ. of Cinti. College of Medicine
1979-84: Assist. Prof., Dept. of Environ. Hlth., Univ. of Cinti. College of Medicine
1981-Present: Director, University of Cincinnati Mass Spectroscopy Consortium Facility
1985-Present: Assoc. Prof. and Director Analytical Chemistry Core Facility, Dept. Environ. Hlth.

Honors and Awards (selected):

Publicly acclaimed by State of Ohio Senate Resolution No.740, Dec. 23, 1981 for research work and scientific accomplishments that have furthered scientific understanding of the biology and chemistry of water pollution. Chairperson, Am. Chem. Soc. and EPA ORD appointed scientific peer review committee to review EPA/EMSL-LV, 1983; Natl. Res. Council, Board of Envtl. Studies and Toxicol. to evaluate exposures to complex mixtures, 1990; Recipient of Distinguished Scientist Lectureship, Marshall University, Huntington, WVA, 1987; Recipient of Toxicology Scholars Lectureship, University of Illinois, Champaign IL, 1988; Visiting Professor, Inst. Biomed. Res., UNAM, Mexico City, 1989; Recipient of Distinguished Alumnus Awards, Emory & Henry College, 1988 and Marshall University, 1990; Recipient of Mexico's Alumni Awards, for contributions to understanding of human health problems associated with environmental contamination, 1990; Visiting Professor, Inst. of Genetics, Fudan University, Shanghai, China, Spring 1992/93; Member, Expert Panel for Office of U.S. Army Surgeon General to evaluate environmental exposures, 1992; Member, Expert Panel for USEPA to evaluate Risk Assessment Program for WTI Incineration Facility, 1993.

Publications (selected):

F. Diaz-Barriga, L.Y. Estrada, J.A. Cuellar and M.W. Tabor, "Exposure of Pregnant Women and Children to Arsenic, Cadmium and Lead from a Smelter in Central Mexico", Bull. Envtl. Contam. Toxicol., in press (1993).

R.-M. Liu, M. Sainsbury, M.W. Tabor, and H.G. Shertzer, "Mechanisms of Protection from Menadione Toxicity by 5, 10-Dihydroindeno[1,2-b]Indole in a Sensitive and Resistant Hepatocyte Line", Biochem. Pharmacol. 46:1491-1499, 1993.

M.W. Tabor, J.L. Xue and A. Chen, editors, Proceedings of International Symposium on Environmental Mutagenesis and Carcinogenesis, Chinese Environ. Mutag. Soc. Press, Shanghai, PRC, 124pp, 1993.

M.W. Tabor, M. Carsiotis, D. Feldhake, P.V. Scarpino, S.T. Giolando and J.C. Loper, "Aerobic Degradation of Sulfonated Azo Dyes by a Gram-Negative Rod, Isolate C7", submitted 1993.

M.W. Tabor, "Environmental Toxicogenetics", In: Professional Practice in Toxicology: A Review, A.M. Warner, D.C. Hohnadel and A.J. Pesce, eds., Am. Assocn. Clin. Chem., Wash., D.C., pp. 573-590 (1993).

M.W. Tabor, "Quality Assurance and Quality Control in Estimates of Environmental Exposures for Human Risk Assessment", Carcinogenesis, Teratogenesis and Mutagenesis 5:56-68 (1993).

M.W. Tabor, J. Eberhard, R. Hutchinson and H.P. Kagen, "The Environmental Persistence, Fate and Biodegradation of Azo Dyes and Aromatic Amines: Physico-Chemical Basis", In: Proc. Environ. Chem. Div. Am. Chem. Soc. 33(2); in press 1993.
